1.  Pledge of Allegiance.

  the Planning Commission on any item on the agenda other than a
  public hearing may do so at this time.

5.  Minute approval for November 5, 2025, Planning Commission meeting.

6.  CONSENT ITEMS:
  a. A six-month time limit extension for the construction of an
  eight-story mixed-use building consisting of 150 residential units,
  commercial/retail space and associated parking on an approximately
  41,000 square-foot H-C (Historic Core) zoned property.

  Recommendation:
  Consider the staff report, any testimony and make a determination.
  It is recommended that you:
  1) Approve the six-month extension for DR24-00058 and
  Resolution No. 2008 dated November 6, 2024; or
  2) Deny the six-month extension for DR24-00058.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS:
  a. A public hearing to consider an application by Raul Cueva, Jr,
  representing IHOP, for Special Use Permit No. 25-00020(SUP25-00020)
  to allow the sale of distilled spirits for on-site consumption
  within an existing restaurant on a C-2A/R-3 zoned property at 4410
  West Century Boulevard.

  A Notice of Exemption (EA-CE-2025-128) has been prepared stating
  that the proposed project is categorically exempt from the
  California Environmental Quality Act, a copy of which is available
  for public review in the Planning Division office of City Hall and
  via email request to faith.smith@cityofinglewood.org.

  Preliminary Recommendations:
  A. If the Planning Commission determines to APPROVE the request,
  it is recommended to:
  1) Affirm the categorical exemption EA-CE-2025-128;
  2) Adopt the resolution approving SUP25-00020.
  B. If the Planning Commision determines to ADD CONDITIONS, it is
  recommended to:
  1) Take the above actions but modify the number of conditions
  as appropriate.
  C. If the Planning Commission determines to DENY the request or
  any part thereof, it is recommended to:
  1) Take the appropriate actions and make the findings.

  recommended to:
  1) Take the above actions but modify the number of conditions

  C. If the Planning Commission determines to DENY the request or
  any part thereof, it is recommended to:
  1) Take the appropriate actions and make the findings.

  within their jurisdiction and not elsewhere considered on the
  agenda may do so at this time.

10.  Commission Initiatives.

Commissioner Trejo, the meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

1.  Thank you to the Planning Commissioners for attending the
  Planning Seminar in Northern California, where we were all
  considered “Stars”! How you were able to see what it is to be
  a Planner, in obtaining information and preparing for Planning
  Commission Meetings, like what our Planners go through monthly.
  You all rose to the occasion and I just wanted to let you know
  how proud of you I am.

  our newest Senior Planner, who joined us today and I wanted her
  to see what and how we conduct a Planning Commission Meeting,
  and so she is here tonight, and Mr. James Perrault, our Planning
  Intern, who has been with us for the last several months and is

6a. SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 24-00026 (SUP24-00026) 401 EAST MANCHESTER
BOULEVARD: A continued public hearing to consider an application by
Gary Le for Special Use Permit No. 24-00026 (SUP24-00026) to allow
the expansion of a drive-thru and construct a 30 square-foot addition
to an existing 3,615 square-foot free-standing fast-food restaurant
that is part of a shopping center on an approximately 58,797 square-
foot H-C (Historic Core) property at 401 East Manchester Boulevard.

Mr. Sean May, Planner, made the staff presentation.

Chairman Springs opened the public  hearing  for  the  Planning
Commissioners to question staff.

Commissioner Rice asked staff –
• So the applicant is going to remove two parking spaces?
• Is there the possibility that a Flashing Yellow Light be posted
  in order to insure the need for a safe Pedestrian Crossing?
  − Mr. May responded to Commissioner Rice’s questions.

Commissioner Trejo asked staff –
• Need correction on how many parking spaces will be lost?
• Employee parking locale at the site – where will and do they
  park their vehicles?
  − Mr. May responded to Commissioner Trejo’s questions.
  − Mr. McCrumby responded to Commissioner Trejo’s question.

Chairman Springs asked staff –
• How far will the billed-up be, is there more than one way to
  exit the site, or is the Manchester driveway the only exit or
  will they have to go through the parking lot area to exit at
  Hillcrest?
  − Mr. May responded to Chairman Springs’ question.
  − Mr. McCrumby responded to Chairman Springs’ question.

Chairman Springs asked the applicant to speak about his project
before the Planning Commission.

Mr. Robert Priest of Design UA, representing the applicant.

Chairman Springs opened the public hearing  for  the  Planning
Commissioners to address the applicant.

• Parking for the general public, will it be reduced?

  landscaping.

None.

6b. SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 25-00002 (SUP25-00002) 1110 WEST
MANCHESTER BOULEVARD: A continued public hearing to consider an
application by Erika Diaz for Special Use Permit No. 25-00015 (SUP25-
00015) to allow the sale of beer and wine for off-site consumption
for an existing service station convenience market on an MU-C (Mixed
Use Corridor) zoned property at 1110 West Manchester Boulevard.

Mr. Brian Espinoza, Assistant Planner, made the staff presentation.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

Commissioner Fowler asked staff –
• When was the last time that a beer and wine license has been
  approved for this area?
• Next question is about the fact that the alcohol would be
  consistently kept in a locked area?
  - Mr. Espinoza responded to Commissioner Fowler’s questions.
  - Mr. McCrumby also responded to Commissioner Fowler’s questions.

Commissioner Rice asked staff –
• How have the crime rates in the area been since 2021?
• Is the Church and School still within the area there?
  - Mr. Espinoza responded to Commissioner Rice’s questions.

Commissioner Trejo asked staff –
• How does the system work with locked cabinet doors, are they near
  to the Emergency Exit, can those cooler cabinets be moved to
  another location in the store?
• Too close to the Emergency exit to make it a quick and easy get-
  away onto the Freeway. Could the Emergency door be kept locked
  also, during business hours?
  - Mr. Espinoza responded to Commissioner Trejo’s questions.
  - Mr. McCrumby also responded to Commissioner Trejo’s questions.

Chairman Springs asked staff –
• Question about the history of this gas station, did it have an
  auto repair also at this location?
  - Mr. Espinoza responded to Chairman Springs’ question.
  - Mr. McCrumby responded to Chairman Springs’ question.

Chairman Springs asked the applicant to come forward and address the
Planning Commission.

Ms. Erica Woods-Diaz of the Woods-Diaz Group and Mr. Nathan, Arco
Gas Station property owner, came forward to address the Planning
Commission.

Commissioner Fowler asked the applicant –
• Where exactly in the store, could the locked coolers be re-
  located, if this were approved?
  - Would you have a problem if maybe we suggested that you come
  in annually, before the planning commission to give a review of
  your progress and to look at your statistics from IPD?
  - Ms. Woods-Diaz responded to Commissioner Fowler’s questions.
  4

  - Mr. Nathan also responded to Commissioner Fowler’s question.

Commissioner Rice asked the applicant –
• How long has the applicant utilized the magnetic locks at their
  stations?
• The type of magnetic process that they are currently using, would
  they improve upon it by changing it?
  - Mr. Nathan responded to Commissioner Rice’s questions.

Commissioner Trejo asked the applicant –
• How does the system work with locked doors, are they near to the
  Emergency Exit, can they be moved to another location in the
  store?
• Too close to the Emergency exit to make it a quick and easy get-
  away onto the Freeway. Could the Emergency door be kept locked
  also, during business hours?
  - Mr. Nathan responded to Commissioner Trejo’s questions.
  - Ms. Woods-Diaz responded to Commissioner Trejo’s questions.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams asked the applicant –
• With regards to the locked doors for the alcohol to reside in, is
  it always locked, and how has that worked for you in the past?
• Why have you decided to have the locked cooler cabinets, are they
  in all of your business locations or how do you justify placing
  them in just a few of your business locations?
  - Mr. Nathan responded to Commissioner Shaw-Williams’ question.

Chairman Springs asked the applicant -
• What is the convenience that you would provide to the
  neighborhood?
• We, the commissioners like to hear from the community, your
  customers, who come out and speak about your project and how it
  will benefit them. Although this evening, there is no here to
  speak on your behalf for your project, why not?
• Chairman Springs asked staff about the location of other
  residences from the Gas Station?
• Also, how could traffic get to the station if they are leaving
  the 405 freeway going North, isn’t there a barrier prohibiting
  traffic from easily crossing Manchester Boulevard to get to the
  station?
  - Mr. Nathan responded to Chairman Springs’ questions.
  - Mr. McCrumby responded to Chairman Springs’ questions to staff.

Chairman Springs opened the floor to hear from the public whether
they are for or against this project.

FOR / AGAINST:
None.

Mr. McCrumby spoke to the Planning Commission and Chairman Springs
to assist with some clarity regarding the applicant’s project.

Chairman Springs called for closing comments from the Planning
Commissioners and asked for a motion from the Planning Commission.

Commissioner Fowler – Comments to the Planning Commission -
• Please consider there is no one in the community opposing this
  applicant to receive a beer and wine license, since this was given
  notice to the community.
• Next, consider there are cameras on site, so the police can see
  who if anything, whom is leaving the store without paying for the
  beer and or wine.

•  Next, consider whoever is attempting to purchase alcohol, must
  show their identification in order to buy it.
•  Please consider whoever is attempting to get the alcohol, the
  coolers are locked until released by the service station
  attendant’s which many cooler are not locked (i.e. 7/11 stores).
•  Consider that this is an established business owner in the
  community and the applicant knows that the convenience of the beer
  and wine is an added bonus for his business as he stated that he
  is aware of the City’s new entertainment aspect that is growing.
•  Consider the convenience of a guest of the community at the Best
  Western, as they can cross the street as opposed to getting into
  their vehicle to drive somewhere else to obtain beer and wine, it
  is a convenience for that person as a hotel guest.
•  My last note here is that I suggest that we require a one year
  review of how his business is going and to see how his police
  reports will show how the business is doing.

Commissioner Rice – Comments to the Planning Commission –
• With regards to this project, initially he was not for it, but in
  listening to the applicant, in seeing how he has taken his other
  project on Imperial Hwy and Yukon, which was a very dilapidated
  building and a poor looking site in the community and the fact
  that you are willing to take a chance on this new project at
  Manchester Boulevard and Ash, especially with the new charging
  station that will be opening across the street, more customers
  will be coming to the city and I feel this will be just what is
  needed at that site.

Commissioner Trejo – Comments to the Planning Commission –
• Wanted to say that she is in agreement with her colleagues and
  for them to understand that she is also on board with their
  suggestions about the approval of this project. Her main concern
  is for security for not only the customers and but also for his
  staff at the store. Hopefully, Mr. Nathan will hire and have more
  employees, especially at night.
• Last she wanted to acknowledge what a great businessman the
  applicant is and what a remarkable job he has already done with
  the Imperial and Yukon site.
• Safety is her main concern and wants to make sure that this is a
  consideration. She feels that with the increase in the smash and
  grabs that are occurring at various small stores it is what is
  heavy on her mind.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams – Comments to the Planning Commission –
• Her concern is not only security but that the property owner will
  take under consideration that we want to make sure that customers
  will not be purchasing alcohol to open and drinking on the
  premises.

Chairman Springs – Comments to the Planning Commission –
• That he feels that the City has an over-concentration of Alcohol,
  Beer and Wine and fails to see the importance of having an
  additional selling location at the applicant’s site.

Chairman Springs asked for a motion from the Planning Commission.

MOTION:
Commissioner Trejo moved that the Planning Commission affirm the
categorical exemption EA-CE-2025-087 and adopt the resolution
approving SUP25-00015, with the added conditions, of changing the
time of beer sales starting at 7:00am to 9:00pm, and also for a
one year review with the Inglewood Police crime statistics and was

Dear City of Inglewood Planning Department,

This letter serves to detail the public convenience and necessity that will be met by
granting a Special Use Permit for IHOP and Applebee’s, to be located at 4410 W
Century Blvd, Inglewood, Ca 90304. We are formally requesting this permit to allow
the sale and dispensing of beer, wine and distilled spirits for on-site consumption as a
full-service restaurant.

Project overview
Our proposed project involves an IHOP and Applebee’s under one roof. A new concept
that will cater to families and visitors. We would like to offer a unique dining experience
not offered anywhere else. With breakfast and delicious steaks, ribs and soups offered
under one umbrella. Our fresh ingredients and delicious food options will always be a
top priority. We are requesting a Special Use Permit to include beer, wine and distilled
spirits service to complement our dining experience.

Public convenience and necessity
We believe that granting this permit is in the public's interest due to the following
reasons:
  1. Economic development and tax revenue: Inglewood 2017 Inc DBA IHOP
  and Applebee’s will contribute to the local economy by hiring full-time and part-
  time employees from the local community with our two-restaurant concept while
  generating additional sales tax revenue for the city and attracting new visitors to
  area and bring business for other local businesses.
  2. Increased choice and access: The proposed service fills a gap in the local
  market. Currently, there is no other establishment of this type within walking
  distance of the residential neighborhood, forcing residents to drive elsewhere for
  similar products or services. This permit would provide the community with
  convenient and safe access to our offerings.
   3. Community enhancement: Our business will serve as a gathering spot and
  community hub for residents and the visiting community. We are committed to
  fostering a positive and safe environment for the patrons and workers.

Community compatibility and mitigation efforts
We understand the need to be a responsible and respectful neighbor. We have taken
the following steps to ensure compatibility with the surrounding area and to mitigate any
potential negative impacts:
  • [Noise]: We will implement measures to minimize noise, such as making sure
  the noise level is always kept inside the premises and making sure our doors are
  closed. We are a family-oriented restaurant and want to make sure families feel
  safe.
  • Parking and traffic: We have accounted for parking needs by providing
  dedicated private on-site parking for 49 vehicles and encouraging employees to
  use public transportation.
  • Safety and security: We will collaborate with local law enforcement to ensure
  our establishment does not increase crime in the area. We have installed exterior
  lighting and security cameras to ensure the safety of everyone outside the
  restaurant.

Conclusion
The special use permit for Inglewood 2017 Inc DBA IHOP and Applebee’s will fulfill a
clear public convenience and necessity, delivering significant community benefits
without negatively impacting the neighborhood. We are confident that our project will be
a valuable and positive addition to the area. We appreciate your consideration of our
application.

BACKGROUND
The Inglewood Municipal Code (IMC), Chapter 12, Article 17.1 Open Space (O-S) Zone,
requires that no new building or structure shall be erected or structurally enlarged within
O-S zoned properties unless the Planning Commission has approved the plans and
drawings.

Existing Conditions
Siminski Park is a neighborhood park located within Council District 3, west of Inglewood
Avenue between 97th Street and 98th Street. The park spans approximately 1.9 acres and
offers a variety of community amenities, including two (2) picnic areas, a playground, a
full basketball court, one (1) restroom facility, and a community center. The park is
accessed by pedestrians and vehicles from Inglewood Avenue and 97 th Street. The park
provides 36 on-site parking spaces.

DISCUSSION
The City proposes enhancements to the park's northeast corner, highlighted by a new
7,500 square-foot community garden, featuring 37 raised wooden beds, 15 tree stump
seats, and a demonstration board. Additional improvements include two (2) concrete pads
with craftsman-style pergolas and picnic tables, a 225 square-foot storage room with an
attached stainless steel sink, eight (8) light poles, a new 80-foot service driveway,
decomposed granite walkways, and new wrought iron fencing and gates to enclose the
garden area.

Garden Operations
The community garden will be open to the public daily, from dusk to dawn. The garden
will provide a variety of fresh produce available for the public to harvest. The Parks and
Recreation Department will maintain the garden area weekly. Produce harvested in the
garden will be available to residents on a first-come, first-serve basis. To ensure quality
and consistent availability of produce, maintenance of the garden beds will be a
collaborative effort between City staff and community members. In the event that
maintenance from the community lags, the City will assume responsibility of maintaining
the garden. The Parks and Recreation Department will periodically host public events in
the demonstration area and provide hands-on learning about gardening, environmental,
and botanical processes.

Site Plan Review Required
The Planning Division has reviewed preliminary plans submitted for the Planning
Commission’s review and determined that they generally comply with the applicable
standards of the IMC. If the Planning Commission approves the request, the applicant will
be required to obtain final plan approval from the Planning Division. The applicant will
also be required to obtain approval for the proposed project from the Building Safety
Division and Public Works Department.
